# Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe

**Qi2** is the open wireless charging standard from the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC). It adds a magnetic ring that snaps the phone into alignment, with charging up to 15W. The Verge notes that Apple contributed MagSafe technology to the standard ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**Qi2.2** (also branded **Qi2 25W**) is the newer version of Qi2. It keeps the magnets but raises the cap to 25W. The WPC says that's nearly 70% more power, and about 0 to 50% in roughly 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). Certified products started appearing in July 2025.

**MagSafe** is Apple's own branding and certification program, not a separate standard. Apple's current MagSafe Charger is certified for Qi2 25W and regular Qi ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m)). According to Macworld, certified MagSafe chargers also have an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify them, plus a magnetometer to prevent compass interference ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). Uncertified "MagSafe-compatible" chargers usually just have magnets and charge at 7.5W.

## What speed you actually get
- **iPhone 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max, 17 series:** up to 25W with a 30W+ adapter ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)).
- **iPhone 16 and 16 Pro:** up to 22.5W. **iPhone Air:** 20W.
- **iPhone 15 and earlier, and 17e:** up to 15W. The iPhone 16e has no MagSafe or Qi2 magnets.
- **Android:** Few phones support Qi2. The Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold get 15W, and the 10 Pro XL gets 25W. Samsung's Galaxy S26 is "Qi2 Ready" and needs a magnetic case ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

## Which to buy
For iPhones, a Qi2 or Qi2.2 charger and a MagSafe charger perform about the same. Macworld found 15W MagSafe and Qi2 chargers evenly matched, and Qi2.2 matches MagSafe at 25W. Look for the Qi2 logo, and buy Qi2.2/25W only if you have a recent iPhone or a Pixel 10 Pro XL. You can verify certification in the [WPC product database](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/).

If you want the simplest option, the [Apple MagSafe Charger (2 m, $49)](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m) is certified for 25W. The adapter is sold separately. Macworld also rounds up third-party options in its [best MagSafe and Qi2 chargers list](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html).

If you tell me which phone you have, I can suggest a specific charger.
